ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Act on Reporting and Using Specified Financial Transaction Information (Korea AML/CFT Act), Financial Action Task Force (FATF) Recommendations as implemented by the Korea Financial Intelligence Unit (KoFIU), Enforcement Decree of the Act on Reporting and Using Specified Financial Transaction Information, Act on Registration of Real Estate Transactions, and the Commercial Act (Korea) regarding corporate governance and shareholder registers.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incorporation (Certificate of Corporation Registration, issued via the Korean Supreme Court Registration Office)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Korean Supreme Court Registration Office / Court Registration Office of the local district court
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille path: issue certificate of good standing and certificate of incorporation from the relevant Korean district court or registry; notarize the corporate representatives signature and then obtain an Apostille from the Korean Ministry of Foreign Affairs for use in an Apostille Convention state. Do not chain consular legalization after the apostille.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing (Corporate Registry Extract)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille path: obtain a certified extract from the court registry, notarize any certified translation, and submit to the Ministry of Foreign Affairs Apostille section. No consular legalization step applies for member states.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Board Resolution or Power of Attorney
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Board of Directors of the Korea Yuhan Hoesa
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarization in Korea, followed either by Hague Apostille for countries party to the Apostille Convention, or, exclusively for non-member states, consular legalization at the relevant foreign consulate in Korea. These two paths are mutually exclusive and must never be applied sequentially.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Articles of Association as amended and certified
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille path: certified true copy of the Articles of Association, notarization, then apostille by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs for Apostille Convention states. For non-member states, perform notarization and then consular legalization at the destination country consulate.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Korean commercial bank maintaining the corporate account
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille path: banker's signature notarized by a Korean notary public, followed by apostille from the Ministry of Foreign Affairs. For non-member states, the reference letter shall be notarized and then legally consularized by the foreign embassy or consulate in Korea; no apostille may be added.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory enhanced due diligence must screen all Ultimate Beneficial Owners, directors and authorized signatories against the United Nations Security Council consolidated sanctions list, OFAC Specially Designated Nationals and Blocked Persons list, EU, HMT UK sanctions list, Korean Ministry of Foreign Affairs sanctions designations, and the KFTC/KoFIU AML blacklists before registration and prior to any dividend flow or capital contribution. KoFIU requires identification of beneficial owners under the Specific Financial Information Act, including foreign politically exposed persons, domestic prominent public officials, family members and close associates; transactions involving non-resident PEPs or any sanctions-linked counterparty require senior management approval, enhanced monitoring, suspicious transaction reporting within 24 hours to KoFIU under Article 4, and a full beneficial ownership chain description through every intermediate entity. Red flags include shell tiering, unexplained nominee relationships, inconsistent passport and corporate data, adverse media, and the use of high-risk jurisdictions; any such finding must terminate or suspend the SPV formation until a clean enhanced screening report is formally recorded.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Korean Supreme Court Registration Office online corporate registration system; entity name availability search through the court registry and the Korea Intellectual Property Rights Information Service (KIPRIS)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The Yuhan Hoesa must have a unique Korean legal name in Hangul script; the Korean commercial registry requires that foreign names be transliterated phonetically into Hangul, and the name must not be identical or confusingly similar to a prior existing corporation, nor may it contain misleading tokens. Official English or Latin-script names may be registered only as transliterations or in a separate English registration record; the statutory naming convention distinguishes trade names, logos, translations, transliterations and foreign-language branch names. All corporate names must follow Korean Commercial Act Article 172-194 and the Registration of Commerce Act.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon name rejection the applicant receives a written or electronic refusal citing the conflicting prior registration or prohibited token. The applicant must file an administrative appeal with the relevant district court registration office or the Supreme Court Registration Office within 14 days, attaching a comparison of the rejected name, evidence of trademark coexistence or consent from the prior holder, and a revised transliteration proposal. If the appeal concerns a ministerial approval token, the applicant must first submit a written clearance opinion from the responsible ministry, and if still denied, an administrative litigation petition to the Administrative Court under the Administrative Litigation Act may be filed within 90 days. During the appeal the applicant may file a new alternative name reservation without losing priority, but the same name cannot be reserved twice within the same rejection queue.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual office or commercial mailbox is generally permissible for a pure equity holding SPV in South Korea as long as the registered office is a physical street address in Korea that is capable of receiving official mail, service of process, tax notices and court documents; however, the Korean National Tax Service, the Financial Supervisory Service and banks may reject a virtual mailbox-only address for VAT registration, corporate bank account opening, financial reporting or if the entity claims substance benefits under treaty. For the ISIC 6420 passive holding SPV, expecting only interbank SWIFT wire and traditional interbank payment rails, the Korea Tax Authority will scrutinize whether the address is not a mere post-office box and whether basic substance steps such as local directors, a filed statutory account, and actual board minutes exist. Ultimate beneficial owners should be prepared to accept a site visit to confirm signage and local records kept at the registered address.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Checklist: (1) verify a clear nameplate or directory listing, (2) verify access to physical board meeting space, (3) keep the statutory ledger, share register and tax records available at the address, (4) confirm a person authorized to receive service of process is accessible, and (5) avoid an address that is used by an unreasonably large number of shell or inactive companies. Quantified risk: low to moderate, approximately 15 to 25 percent in the first three years for a passive SPV, increasing to greater than 50 percent if the company receives intercompany dividends, claims tax treaty benefits or files annual corporate tax returns with zero employees and no local bank account; Korean municipal district tax offices occasionally conduct unannounced field inspections and may report suspicious lack of substance to the National Tax Service and KoFIU.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Commercial Act of South Korea (상법), Articles 287-287-2 (establishment of limited liability company), Article 288 (articles of incorporation), Article 290 (subscription of shares), Article 292 (registration of incorporation), Article 295 (registration of directors), and Article 317 (registration of company).
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registration Division of the Local District Court (법원등기국) having territorial jurisdiction over the registered office address; for Seoul, the Seoul Central District Court Registration Division.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Articles of Incorporation (정관) and Certificate of Incorporation Registration (법인설립등기신청서) filed with the court registry.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: None. South Korean law does not impose a minimum paid-up capital requirement for a Yuhan Hoesa (limited liability company). However, the total issued shares must be fully paid in at the time of incorporation, and the paid-in amount must be deposited into a temporary bank account in the name of the company or its incorporator, with a certificate of deposit issued by the bank. The funds are released only upon completion of incorporation registration.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en:
RESOLUTION OF THE FIRST BOARD OF DIRECTORS OF YUHANGHOESA (LIMITED LIABILITY COMPANY) ADOPTED BY UNANIMOUS WRITTEN CONSENT IN LIEU OF A MEETING PURSUANT TO ARTICLE 287-2 AND ARTICLE 368 OF THE COMMERCIAL ACT OF SOUTH KOREA

WHEREAS, the undersigned, being all of the directors of Yuhan Hoesa (the 'Company'), a limited liability company duly organized under the laws of the Republic of Korea, have consented to the adoption of the following resolutions without a formal meeting, as permitted by law and the Company's Articles of Incorporation;

NOW, THEREFORE, BE IT RESOLVED, effective as of the date of this resolution, as follows:

1. SUBSCRIPTION AND ALLOTMENT OF SHARES: The Board hereby ratifies and confirms the subscription and allotment of the entire initial share capital of the Company, consisting of 100,000 common shares with a par value of KRW 1,000 each, for a total issued and paid-up capital of KRW 100,000,000 (approximately USD 75,000). The Board acknowledges that each subscriber has fully paid the subscription price in cash, and the corresponding deposit certificate has been issued by the designated bank. The Board directs the Chief Executive Officer to file the certificate of incorporation with the competent District Court Registry and to take all necessary steps to complete the statutory registration.

2. ADOPTION OF ARTICLES OF INCORPORATION: The Board adopts and ratifies the Articles of Incorporation of the Company, as previously executed by the incorporators, which set forth the corporate name, purpose, registered office, share structure, and governance provisions. The Board directs that a certified copy of the Articles be attached to the incorporation filing and that any subsequent amendments be made only in accordance with the Commercial Act.

3. REGISTERED OFFICE: The Board designates the registered office of the Company at 123 Teheran-ro, Gangnam-gu, Seoul, Republic of Korea, and authorizes the Chief Executive Officer to execute any lease or service agreements necessary to maintain such office and to notify the National Tax Service and the court registry of the address.

4. APPOINTMENT OF STATUTORY OFFICERS: The Board appoints the following individuals to serve in the capacities indicated, each to hold office until the next annual general meeting of shareholders or until their successors are duly elected and qualified: (a) Mr. Kim Min-jun as Chief Executive Officer and Representative Director, with full authority to represent the Company in all transactions, sign contracts, and open bank accounts; (b) Ms. Lee Soo-ah as Chief Financial Officer, with authority to manage financial records, sign tax filings, and oversee treasury operations; and (c) Mr. Park Ji-hoon as Compliance Officer, responsible for ensuring adherence to the Commercial Act, the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act, and all applicable anti-money laundering regulations.

5. BANKING AUTHORIZATION: The Board authorizes the opening of corporate bank accounts with Shinhan Bank and Woori Bank, and designates the Chief Executive Officer and Chief Financial Officer as joint signatories for all wire transfers, withdrawals, and other banking transactions. The Board further authorizes the use of SWIFT wire and traditional interbank payment rails for dividend distributions and intercompany funding, subject to the Company's internal control policies.

6. CORPORATE SEAL AND DOCUMENTATION: The Board approves the adoption of a corporate seal (법인인감) and authorizes the Chief Executive Officer to register the seal with the court registry and to use it for all official documents, contracts, and filings. The Board further directs that all corporate records, including the share register, minutes, and financial statements, be maintained at the registered office in accordance with Article 396 of the Commercial Act.

7. GENERAL AUTHORIZATION: The Board authorizes any officer of the Company to execute, deliver, and file all documents, pay all fees, and take all actions necessary to effectuate the incorporation of the Company and the opening of its operations, including but not limited to tax registration with the National Tax Service, business license application with the local district office, and any other regulatory filings required by law.

This resolution is effective immediately and shall be filed with the corporate records of the Company. All actions taken by the officers of the Company prior to the date of this resolution in connection with the incorporation are hereby ratified and confirmed.

ADOPTED this [date] by the unanimous written consent of the Board of Directors.

[Signature of Director 1] [Signature of Director 2] [Signature of Director 3]

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Reservation of Corporate Name and Pre-incorporation Checks
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Supreme Court Registration Office (대법원 등기국) via the online portal 'I-RO' (인터넷등기소)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Conduct a name search on the I-RO system to ensure the proposed corporate name 'Yuhan Hoesa' is not identical or confusingly similar to any existing registered company in Korea. The name must include the legal suffix '유한회사' (Yuhan Hoesa) to indicate limited liability. After confirming availability, reserve the name for a period of 30 days. Simultaneously, prepare the Articles of Incorporation in Korean, notarized by a notary public, and obtain a certificate of deposit for the paid-up capital from a domestic bank. The deposit must be made into a temporary account in the name of the company or its incorporator, and the bank will issue a certificate of deposit (예금증명서) confirming the amount. This step is critical to avoid rejection at the registry.
required_dossiers: Completed name search result from I-RO
Certificate of deposit for paid-up capital from a Korean bank
Passport copies of all incorporators and directors
Power of attorney if using a local agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is rejected due to similarity, immediately select an alternative name and re-submit. If the deposit certificate is defective, obtain a corrected certificate from the bank. If the notarization is incomplete, re-notarize the Articles with the notary.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execution and Notarization of Articles of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Local Notary Public (공증인) and the District Court Registration Division
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Finalize the Articles of Incorporation in Korean, including the corporate purpose (passive holding of subsidiary shares and corporate dividends), share structure, registered office address, and governance provisions. All incorporators must sign the Articles before a notary public, who will certify the signatures and the legality of the document. The notarized Articles are a mandatory attachment to the incorporation registration. After notarization, prepare the registration application form (법인설립등기신청서) and attach the notarized Articles, the certificate of deposit, and the identification documents of the directors. Submit the complete package to the Registration Division of the District Court with territorial jurisdiction over the registered office. The court will review the documents for compliance with the Commercial Act and issue a certificate of incorporation registration (등기사항증명서) upon approval.
required_dossiers: Certificate of deposit for paid-up capital
Identification documents of all directors and incorporators
Power of attorney if filed by an agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the court issues a query (보정명령) due to missing or incorrect information, correct the deficiencies within the given period (usually 2 weeks) and re-submit. If the application is rejected, file a new application with the corrected documents. If the notarization is defective, re-execute the Articles and re-notarize.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Registration of Incorporation with the District Court Registry
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registration Division of the Local District Court (법원등기국)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After the court accepts the application, the registration officer will review the submission and, if satisfied, enter the company into the commercial registry. The registration fee (approximately KRW 300,000) must be paid via revenue stamps or electronic payment. Upon completion, the court issues a Certificate of Registered Matters (등기사항증명서) which serves as conclusive evidence of the company's legal existence. This certificate is required for all subsequent steps, including tax registration and bank account opening. The company must also register its corporate seal (법인인감) with the court, which will be used for official documents. The entire process typically takes 3-5 business days after submission.
required_dossiers: Certificate of deposit for paid-up capital
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the court suspends the registration due to a defect, the applicant will receive a notice of correction. Correct the issue and re-submit within the statutory deadline. If the fee is insufficient, pay the balance immediately. If the seal registration is incomplete, complete the seal registration before the court closes the file.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Tax Registration and Business License Application
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: National Tax Service (국세청) and the Local District Office (구청)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Within 20 days of incorporation, file for corporate tax registration with the National Tax Service (NTS) using the certificate of registered matters. Obtain a corporate tax identification number (사업자등록번호) by submitting the application form, the certificate of registered matters, and the corporate seal. The NTS will issue a business registration certificate (사업자등록증) which is required for opening bank accounts and issuing tax invoices. Additionally, if the company has a physical office, register with the local district office for the local business license (사업장 신고). For a pure holding company, no industrial license is required, but the business registration must reflect the holding activity. The NTS will also assign a tax code for VAT and corporate income tax purposes. This step is critical for compliance with the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act if the company receives foreign investment.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the NTS queries the application due to incomplete information, respond within the given period. If the business registration is delayed, request expedited processing. If the office lease is not recognized, provide a certificate of address or a notarized lease agreement.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Bank Account Opening and Corporate Seal Registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Commercial Banks (e.g., Shinhan Bank, Woori Bank) and the District Court Registry
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a corporate bank account with a Korean commercial bank by presenting the certificate of registered matters, the corporate seal certificate, the business registration certificate, and the identification of the authorized signatories. The bank will verify the company's existence and the authority of the signatories. For a holding company, the bank will conduct enhanced due diligence under the Financial Transactions Reports Act, requiring a declaration of the ultimate beneficial owner and the source of funds. The bank will also set up SWIFT wire capabilities for international transfers. Simultaneously, ensure the corporate seal is registered with the court registry, as it is required for all banking and legal documents. The bank may require a minimum deposit, but this is not a statutory requirement.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank rejects the application due to AML concerns, provide additional documentation on the source of funds and the corporate structure. If the bank requires a physical visit, schedule an appointment. If the seal certificate is not accepted, obtain a new seal certificate from the court.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not Applicable - The entity is a pure equity holding SPV under ISIC 6420, which does not involve physical manufacturing, chemical processing, assembly, or warehousing. No industrial licensing is required.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Not Applicable - No physical operations or emissions. The company does not require an Environmental Impact Assessment under the Environmental Impact Assessment Act of South Korea.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not Applicable - No wastewater, VOC, or hazardous waste generation. The company is a passive holding entity with no industrial discharge.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Not Applicable - The company does not operate a physical facility. However, the registered office must comply with the Building Act and fire safety regulations for commercial offices, including a basic fire extinguisher and evacuation plan. The local district office may require a fire safety inspection for the office space, but this is a landlord responsibility. No Civil Defense permit is required for a holding company.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: National Tax Service of the Republic of Korea, operating the HomeTax electronic tax administration portal; export-clearance matching is performed with Korea Customs Service under the Ministry of Economy and Finance.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For a foreign-owned Yuhan Hoesa, the foreign non-resident entity first forms the Korean limited company at the competent district court registry. The company must then file a business registration application with the National Tax Service district tax office that has jurisdiction over its registered place of business no later than 20 days from incorporation or commencement of business; the standard filing requests a 10-digit business registration number that simultaneously functions as the corporate enterprise taxpayer ID, VAT registration ID, and withholding tax account number. Required evidentiary package includes the corporate registration certificate issued by the court registry, articles of incorporation, proof of registered address, identity and passport documents of the legal representative, and, where applicable, the foreign investment certificate issued under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act. If the foreign non-resident has no local place of business and no Korean subsidiary, it may use a tax representative under the Framework Act on National Taxes to obtain a business registration number for VAT withholding, e-invoicing, and refund purposes from the tax office with jurisdiction over that tax representative, depending on National Tax Service practice. The issued registration certificate confirms the legal entity classification as a domestic corporation for corporate tax and as a VAT-registered enterprise for indirect tax purposes.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Korean tax law does not provide a check-the-box pass-through election or a hybrid-mismatch election for a Yuhan Hoesa. The company remains a domestic corporation taxed at entity level on worldwide income. Available non-classification elections include the domestic consolidated tax return regime for a resident parent corporation and its 100% domestically incorporated subsidiaries, an election for the foreign dividend deduction, and ordinary foreign tax credit and tax-treaty relief elections; none changes the entity-level classification.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value Added Tax (VAT) under the South Korean VAT Act, administered by the National Tax Service through the HomeTax electronic system and coordinated with Korea Customs Service for export clearance.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: KRW 0; no monetary VAT registration exemption applies to a domestic incorporated Yuhan Hoesa. Business registration must be submitted within 20 days of business commencement, and the resulting business registration certificate includes the mandatory VAT registration identifier. A pure equity holding SPV holding passive shares and receiving corporate dividends is registered for VAT administration purposes but has no VAT output tax liability on dividend receipts because dividends are outside the scope of VAT. Small-business simplified VAT filing rules do not create an exemption threshold for corporations.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: VAT-registered entities must issue electronic tax invoices through the National Tax Service HomeTax electronic tax invoice system for every taxable supply to another VAT-registered business. Transaction details must be transmitted to tax administration in near real time through the mandated electronic tax invoice clearance channel; the National Tax Service validates and assigns a digital invoice number and digital signature preserving a fiscal anti-fraud stamp. Businesses subject to the mandate must integrate their ERP, accounting, or billing systems with the National Tax Service application programming interface or use the HomeTax portal, and every electronic tax invoice must contain the zero-rate or standard-rate code, supplier and customer business registration numbers, supply value, VAT amount, and export declaration identifier where applicable. Paper invoices are reserved for prescribed exceptional cases; intentionally issuing forged, duplicated, or untransmitted tax invoices triggers the electronic invoice fraud penalty provisions. The mandatory cash receipt system supplements VAT control for B2C payments where a customer requests a cash receipt.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Goods exported from South Korea are zero-rated under the VAT Act only where an electronic export declaration has been filed with Korea Customs Service, the goods actually leave the Korean customs territory within the statutory period, and the export proceeds are repatriated in a foreign-exchange settlement transaction to Korea in the name of the exporting enterprise. Offshore services supplied to non-residents are zero-rated where the place of supply is outside Korea; for digital services, the place of supply rules apply and the supplier must retain evidence of consumer residence and foreign payment. For the ISIC 6420 pure equity holding SPV, dividend receipts from subsidiary shares are not supplies at all for VAT, so they are neither taxable nor zero-rated; if the SPV later licenses intangibles or sells services abroad, the same export zero-rating evidence set is required.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Korea Customs Service electronic export declaration (customs clearance certificate, commonly evidencing the exporter, shipper, commodity code, quantity, and FOB value)
Commercial invoice issued by the exporting entity
Packing list and transport documents such as the bill of lading or air waybill
Foreign exchange settlement confirmation / inward remittance certificate (FIRC) issued by a Korean Foreign Exchange Bank
Zero-rated export electronic tax invoice with the export declaration number inserted
Foreign buyer purchase order or contract if requested in a refund audit
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The National Tax Service automatically cross-matches zero-rating claims against Korea Customs Service export declarations, electronic tax invoices, and foreign exchange bank settlement data. If a zero-rated supply is not supported by the required customs or foreign-exchange documentation, or if export proceeds are not repatriated within the mandatory 180-day foreign-exchange settlement window and no lawful extension has been approved, the 0% rate is retroactively overturned. The Korean exporter must repay the input VAT previously attributed or offset, pay 10% output VAT on the export price, and is liable for statutory penalty surcharges under the Framework Act on National Taxes, including understatement or unfaithful return penalties and the statutory daily late-payment penalty. Intentional fabrication of export declarations, bills of lading, or FIRCs is punishable under the Punishment of Tax Evaders Act with imprisonment and fines, and the retrospective clawback follows the ordinary VAT correction period, extended for fraudulent omission. Any VAT refund already issued is recovered with statutory interest.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Korea (BOK), acting under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act; the Ministry of Economy and Finance retains broad foreign-exchange policy oversight and issuing authority for key public notices.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: South Korea operates a liberalized but closely supervised convertibility regime under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act. Current-account transactions, such as dividends, royalties, trade payments, and operational disbursements, are fully convertible and require only standard bank verification of underlying supporting documents. Capital-account transactions, including inbound equity subscriptions, cross-border borrowing, and investment from the holding SPV, remain subject to a risk-based reporting and approval system administered by the Bank of Korea through designated foreign exchange banks. Foreign capital can generally be wired into a domestic KRW or foreign-currency account without a shutdown period, but the corresponding FX trade reporting code must be accurately filed and the bank must validate the underlying transaction. There is no statutory surrender of export proceeds; Korean resident exporters may retain foreign exchange in domestic foreign-currency deposit accounts. For a non-resident shareholder injecting equity into a Yuhan Hoesa, the practical hurdles are mostly documentary and compliance-driven rather than discretionary: capital verification requires an actual receipt of funds, a bank-issued foreign currency trading certificate, and corporate registration amendments filed within the statutory deadline. Dividend repatriation requires evidence of distributable reserves, corporate tax filing confirmation, applicable withholding tax remittance, and the mandatory reporting of outward remittance. Bank compliance committees scrutinize the economic substance behind a passive holding SPV. Therefore, day-to-day convertibility is high for established treasury flows, but AML and beneficial-ownership documentation gaps can delay both capital contributions and profit remittances if the holding SPV lacks a transparent corporate structure and clean source-of-funds proof.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act and its enforcement decree, export proceeds must be collected through a designated foreign exchange bank within 18 months from the date the export declaration is accepted, unless the Bank of Korea grants a justified extension. There is currently no mandatory conversion ratio or surrender requirement; the exporter may choose to maintain foreign currency receipts in a foreign-currency deposit account. If the SPV or its operating export subsidiaries require KRW liquidity, conversion is executed at prevailing market rates through a licensed bank and must be recorded under the appropriate macroeconomic foreign-exchange transaction code.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Basic Operational KRW Account / Foreign-Currency Deposit Account / Capital Escrow Account
Capital Escrow Account / Basic Operational Current Account / FX Settlement Account
Capital Escrow Account / Basic Operational KRW Account / Foreign-Currency Account
Basic Operational Currency Account / Capital Escrow Account

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Offshore digital EMIs are not viable for this Korean corporate treasury mandate. Under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act and prudential banking rules, only financial institutions licensed in South Korea and registered with the Financial Supervisory Service may conduct corporate foreign-exchange business, open KRW settlement accounts, access domestic interbank clearing rails, or file the mandatory FX transaction codes with the Bank of Korea. Offshore fintech EMIs cannot provide a legally valid Korean corporate account, cannot execute statutory capital verification, and cannot report equity or trade-related foreign-exchange transactions on behalf of a resident Yuhan Hoesa. Therefore, the client must use a domestic Tier-1 commercial bank for all KRW-denominated and cross-border settlement activity.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical in-branch presence is generally mandatory for corporate account onboarding. At a minimum, the statutorily registered representative of the Yuhan Hoesa must appear in person at the designated bank branch for identity verification and the AML/CFT interview. For non-resident directors, remote consular proxy opening is not uniformly accepted; most Korean banks require personal appearance or, in exceptional cases, an approved resident finance officer holding a notarized power of attorney and an original board resolution. Enhanced due-diligence interviews are required for a passive holding SPV, and video-call interviews may supplement but cannot fully replace the statutory physical identification process.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Large inbound equity subscription from a foreign parent with no clear correlating board resolution or share-subscription documentation.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Notarized board resolution from the ultimate parent, certified share subscription agreement, corporate registration chart, shareholders' register, source-of-funds statement, recent audited financial statements of the parent, bank reference letter, and certified passport of the shareholder. A legal opinion confirming the validity of the equity injection and the authority of the signing officers should also be provided.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Passive holding SPV with layered foreign intermediate holdcos obscuring the ultimate beneficial owner.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: A complete transparent corporate chart from ultimate beneficial owner to the Korean Yuhan Hoesa, OECD CRS self-certification forms, business registration certificates and registry extracts for every intermediate entity, passports or national IDs of all natural-person UBOs, and a professional legal or tax advisor's opinion explaining the commercial or tax rationale for the intermediate layers.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: UBO or named director appears in PEP, negative-media, or sanctions screening lists.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Independent PEP and sanctions screening clearance from a reputable screening provider, documented explanation of any flagged matches, government-issued identity documents, proof of reputation rehabilitation or official clearance letters, enhanced due-diligence questionnaire, high-net-worth source-of-wealth declaration, and a commitment letter for ongoing transaction monitoring.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Apparent inconsistency between declared passive holding purpose and actual treasury flows, such as anticipated trade disbursements, intercompany loans, or intellectual-property royalty remittances.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Detailed treasury management plan, complete set of intercompany agreements covering any future trade, financing, or royalty transactions, projected dividend flow forecasts, historical audited financial statements, Korean corporate tax filings, board resolutions authorizing each anticipated disbursement class, and transactional purpose-code explanation letters acceptable to the bank compliance committee.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: For a compliant inbound capital injection into the Yuhan Hoesa, the wiring bank must debit the overseas parent account and route funds via SWIFT MT103 to the SPV's designated domestic account at a licensed Korean bank. The remitter must be identical to the subscribing shareholder and the FX purpose code must identify an inward equity investment or foreign direct investment. The Korean bank will require the corporate registration certificate, board resolution, share subscription documentation, and source-of-funds evidence before posting value. After receipt, the bank issues a foreign currency trading certificate for capital verification purposes, the relevant capital increase is registered with the Korean corporate registry, and the foreign-exchange report is filed with the Bank of Korea through the bank within the regulatory timeline. Funds should not be commingled with trade receivable proceeds or operating income in the capital escrow account.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound treasury disbursements should be cleared using SWIFT MT103 for operating expenses, intercompany service fees, dividends, and other non-trade payments. Physical trade settlements should be structured through commercial letters of credit governed by UCP600 or documentary collections, supported by invoices, bills of lading, packing lists, customs declarations, and the relevant FX purpose codes. The Korean bank executes cross-border legs through its correspondent banking network, while domestic KRW clearing between local accounts operates through BOK-Wire and the banking settlement infrastructure. All outgoing payments must undergo transaction screening and be supported by signed board-approved disbursement instructions.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable KRW forward contracts with a licensed Korean foreign-exchange bank, executed only when the SPV or its operating subsidiaries have an underlying receivables, payables, dividend, or trade exposure

Cross-currency swaps approved by the Polish? no - validated by licensed Korean banks to hedge foreign-currency equity injections or external debt exposure, provided the underlying transaction is real and fully documented
Registered FX options for commercial exposure with documentary purpose-code support and no speculative leverage

Offshore KRW non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) are not a recommended primary instrument for the domestic Korean entity; they may be considered only as a supplementary hedge under a separately approved treasury policy and only with a credible underlying exposure

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Corporate Income Tax Return and attached financial statements under Article 60 of the Corporate Tax Act
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 3 months after the fiscal year-end; for a December 31 fiscal year-end, no later than March 31 of the following year; a one-month extension to April 30 is available where a certified independent audit is required or a foreign tax extension is granted.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file triggers a 20% negligence penalty on the unpaid corporate income tax, or 10% for an underreported filed return, plus a daily late-payment surcharge of approximately 0.03% on the delinquent tax; prolonged non-payment and non-filing expose the SPV to enforced tax collection, bank account attachment, tax lien registration, and potential court-led administrative dissolution and strike-off from the commercial register.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Local Income Tax Return on corporate income tax surcharge under the Local Tax Act
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Municipal or provincial tax authority of the registered business address, such as the Seoul Metropolitan Government tax bureau
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 3 months after the fiscal year-end, aligned with the corporate tax return; for a calendar-year entity, the filing deadline is March 31, and it follows any valid extension to April 30 for audited companies.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file or underreporting triggers a local negligence penalty of 10% to 20% of the unpaid local income tax, plus a daily late-payment interest charge on the arrears; continued delinquency may result in compulsory local tax collection, attachment of corporate bank accounts, and cancellation of business registration by the local authority.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Foreign-Invested Enterprise Annual Business Report and Beneficial Ownership Change Report under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Invest Korea / KOTRA on behalf of the Ministry of Trade, Industry and Energy, plus the designated Foreign Exchange Bank for transactional reporting
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: The foreign-invested enterprise annual business report is due within 90 days after the close of the fiscal year, i.e., March 31 for a December 31 year-end; any acquisition, transfer, or disposal of shares or membership quotas by a foreign investor must be reported within 30 days of the transaction date.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file the annual business report or a 30-day share-transfer report is subject to administrative fines under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act; misleading or omitted foreign ownership information may also trigger foreign exchange penalty provisions, loss of foreign-invest-enterprise status, and administrative enforcement proceedings.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual General Meeting of Members, Approval of Financial Statements, and Maintenance of the Corporate Minute Book
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Internal corporate governance record; not filed with a governmental authority but must be physically available at the registered office
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: The regular meeting of members must be convened and financial statements approved within 1 month after the end of each fiscal year; for a December 31 fiscal year-end, the deadline is January 31 of the following year.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-convening of the annual members' meeting or non-preparation of statutory minutes subjects each responsible director to an administrative fine of up to KRW 5 million under the Korean Commercial Act; persistent failure to maintain statutory records can lead to a court-appointed inspector, shareholder remedies, and in extreme dormant-company cases, court-led dissolution and administrative strike-off.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Certified Independent Auditor's Report and Audit Appointment Documentation, if the entity meets the external audit mandate
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Financial Supervisory Service and, where applicable, the National Tax Service as part of the corporate tax return package
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: The independent auditor must be appointed no later than 45 days before the fiscal year-end; the audited financial statements and auditor's report must be finalized and submitted within 4 months after the fiscal year-end, i.e., April 30 for a December 31 year-end, with the AGM approval by January 31.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to appoint an auditor or obstruction of the audit is subject to administrative fines under the Act on External Audit of Stock Companies, Etc.; unaudited financial statements will be rejected for corporate tax filing purposes, triggering the 20% negligence penalty and daily late-payment interest, and can result in formal regulatory corrective orders and criminal penalties against directors.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: An independent certified CPA audit is mandatory for a Korean Yuhan Hoesa LLC if the company is listed on a Korean securities market or if the company's total assets as of the end of the immediately preceding fiscal year are KRW 12 billion or more, approximately USD 8.9 million, based on the consolidated balance sheet where applicable. There is no separate statutory turnover or headcount trigger under the general external audit law for a private LLC; however, if the SPV holds subsidiaries in regulated industries such as banking, insurance, securities, or asset management, a statutory audit is required regardless of asset size. In addition, the National Tax Service may require a certified CPA audit report where the entity's book records are deemed inadequate or where foreign tax credit, transfer pricing, or tax-exempt dividend positions are claimed.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: The applicable framework is Korean IFRS (K-IFRS as adopted by the Korean Accounting Standards Board) for companies meeting the external audit threshold or operating in regulated sectors; a non-listed Yuhan Hoesa LLC that is not subject to mandatory external audit may apply the General Korean Accounting Standards for Non-Public Companies, commonly referred to as Korean GAAP, or may elect to adopt K-IFRS. Auditors must conduct the engagement in accordance with Korean Standards on Auditing and independence requirements of the Act on External Audit of Stock Companies, Etc.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Korea does not require a private Yuhan Hoesa LLC to file a separate annual beneficial ownership return in the ordinary course. Instead, beneficial ownership is confirmed through the statutory register of members, the commercial registration update filed with the Korean registry court upon any quota transfer, and, where the SPV is a foreign-invested enterprise, the 30-day reporting window to the Foreign Exchange Bank or Invest Korea for any shareholding transfer, acquisition, or pledge. The annual foreign-invested enterprise business report must identify the foreign investor and the current shareholding structure. Further, under financial transaction and AML rules, the SPV must promptly provide true beneficial ownership information to its bank, financial institution, or the Korea Financial Intelligence Unit upon lawful request; failure to maintain current member and ultimate shareholder data may trigger denial of banking services, foreign exchange sanctions, and civil monetary penalties.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 3,500 - 10,000 per year, subject to consolidated SPV complexity and subsidiary count

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 24% national top corporate tax rate under Corporate Tax Act Article 55(1), plus a 10% local income tax surcharge producing a combined top effective rate of 26.4%
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No free-zone patent box or general tax holiday applies to a passive equity holding SPV; qualifying inter-corporate dividends may be deducted in part under the dividend-received deduction rules, and foreign-source dividend taxes may be relieved through the indirect foreign tax credit under Corporate Tax Act Article 57

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Corporate Income Tax Return (CIT Return) with Statement of Tax Adjustments and financial statement schedules, submitted through the National Tax Service HomeTax electronic filing portal
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual; semi-annual interim corporate tax prepayments are required under Article 63 of the Corporate Tax Act
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Article 60 of the Corporate Tax Act requires filing within three months after the end of the fiscal year; for a calendar-year SPV the statutory deadline is 31 March of the following year, with a limited extension by application

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Legal name, registration number, fiscal year-end, head office location, place of effective management, and Korean domestic business place or resident agent details
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A pure equity holding SPV must clearly declare its Korean domestic place of business or, if it only receives passive Korean-source income, indicate that it is a foreign corporation subject to withholding rather than full corporate assessment; misdescribing a permanent establishment can trigger secondary tax liability

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Line 2 - Gross Income and Non-Taxable Income
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: All revenues including foreign and domestic dividends, interest, capital gains from equity disposals, and non-taxable or exempt income categories
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Foreign subsidiary dividends are includible unless a specific deduction or exclusion applies; attach share ownership certificates, dividend resolutions, and foreign withholding documents when claiming an indirect foreign tax credit or dividend-received deduction

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Line 3 - Deductions, Losses, and Tax-Base Adjustments
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Ordinary expenses, depreciation, bad debts, net operating loss carryforwards, and transfer pricing adjustments
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Intercompany management fees, interest, and service charges paid by the SPV must satisfy the arm's length standard and must be backed by contracts, invoices, evidence of actual services, and board approvals; passive holding SPVs with no staff or activity cannot deduct fabricated charges without fatal exposure

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Line 4 - Foreign Tax Credit and Domestic Tax Relief
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Computation of foreign tax credit for foreign-source income and any withholding tax credits
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Use Article 57 of the Corporate Tax Act; the credit is limited to the Korean corporate tax attributable to foreign-source income, and the SPV must attach foreign tax assignment schedules and payment proofs; excessive claimed credits are a common audit trigger for non-resident holding vehicles

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Schedule of intercompany sales, purchases, loans, interest, royalties, services, and equity transactions with connected persons
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Disclose all controlled cross-border transactions; if the SPV fails to attach the required transfer pricing documentation or gives incomplete beneficial ownership data, the NTS may reassess income under the arm's length principle and impose penalties

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Line 6 - Withholding Tax and Payable Tax
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Computation of tax after withholding credits, interim payments, and refunds, and declaration of taxes withheld on outbound payments
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If the SPV pays outbound dividends, interest, or royalties to non-resident shareholders or lenders, declare the statutory 22% withholding; to apply a reduced Korea DTA rate, attach the recipient's Tax Residency Certificate and beneficial ownership statement to the return

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing attracts penalty tax under the Framework Act on Taxes; unfaithful or understated returns attract 20% to 40% of the unpaid tax depending on negligence or fraud, plus statutory late-payment interest; intentional fraudulent non-filing is prosecuted under Article 3(1) of the Punishment of Tax Evaders Act with imprisonment not exceeding two years or a fine not exceeding twice the evaded tax

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 22% on outbound dividends paid by a Korean corporation to a non-resident shareholder, comprised of 20% national withholding plus 2% local income tax surcharge; a Korea DTA may reduce the rate, typically to 5-10% for substantial shareholding and 15% for portfolio holdings
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: The non-resident recipient must prove treaty residence, beneficial ownership, and entitlement to the benefits; the recipient must supply a valid Tax Residency Certificate from the treaty jurisdiction, a signed beneficial ownership declaration, and the prescribed NTS application for non-resident withholding reduction or exemption before the payment date; if the documents are not submitted on time, the payer must withhold at 22% and the recipient can claim a refund at the competent district tax office within the statutory refund period
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory rates for outbound interest and royalties are also 22% (20% national plus 2% local surtax); under many Korea DTAs the withholding rate is reduced to approximately 10% for interest and 5-15% for royalties, subject to beneficial ownership, absence of a Korean permanent establishment, and substance requirements

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Local File is mandatory when aggregate cross-border related-party transactions exceed KRW 5 billion; Master File is mandatory when group consolidated revenue exceeds KRW 100 billion and foreign related-party transactions exceed KRW 5 billion; the NTS may request contemporaneous evidence for any lower-value transaction where the price is not arm's length
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Korea does not maintain a separate Economic Substance Regulations reporting regime, but Article 4 of the International Tax Adjustment Act, the CFC rules, and treaty beneficial ownership doctrines require genuine commercial substance; for a pure equity holding SPV, the Core Income-Generating Activities are acquisition, holding, financing, management, and disposal decisions over the subsidiary shares, and those functions must be performed by the Korean board with offices, records, bank accounts, personnel, and board minutes in Korea

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The pure equity holding SPV omits foreign or domestic dividend income from the CIT Return, fabricates deductible management or financing expenses, or files nil or negative taxable income while still distributing cash to shareholders without arm's length return
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Article 3(1) of the Punishment of Tax Evaders Act penalizes fraud or other unlawful acts to evade corporate tax by imprisonment not exceeding two years or a fine not exceeding twice the evaded tax; the understated amount is also subject to a 40% unlawful understatement penalty under the Framework Act on Taxes plus statutory late-payment interest
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who sign or cause the false return can be treated as secondary tax obligors under Article 12 of the National Tax Collection Act, exposing their personal assets to civil execution, a travel ban (Blacklisting), and individual criminal imprisonment for tax evasion

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The SPV claims reduced dividend, interest, or royalty withholding under a Korea DTA based only on a Tax Residency Certificate while the non-resident parent lacks beneficial ownership, assumes no risk, and the Korean board exercises no substantive control or business purpose over the passive income flow
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Article 4 of the International Tax Adjustment Act allows the NTS to disregard the conduit and recharacterize the income; Corporate Tax Act Article 98(2) then requires the full 22% statutory withholding, additional tax penalties up to 40% for fraudulent understatement, and criminal prosecution under Article 3(1) of the Punishment of Tax Evaders Act if the DTA claim is intentional and fraudulent
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and officers acting as withholding agents are personally liable for taxes withheld or under-withheld; personal bank accounts and property may be seized, travel officials may impose a travel ban (Blacklisting), and intentional participation in the conduit scheme carries criminal imprisonment

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company / AML and Beneficial Ownership Concealment
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The Korean SPV has no staff, physical office, separate bank account, board meeting minutes, share register, or accounting records, is funded solely through unexplained related-party loans, and uses nominee directors to conceal the ultimate beneficial owner while moving high-value dividends and proceeds
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Incomplete or false beneficial ownership and suspicious transaction reporting violates the Act on Reporting and Use of Certain Financial Transaction Information, carrying criminal fines and imprisonment under the AML and proceeds-of-crime laws; the shell arrangement is also attacked under Article 4 of the International Tax Adjustment Act and Article 3(1) of the Punishment of Tax Evaders Act as an unlawful scheme to conceal taxable income
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Nominee and de facto directors cannot use corporate separateness to avoid liability; courts can order civil restitution of diverted assets, confiscate criminal proceeds, impose departure restrictions and a travel ban (Blacklisting), and impose personal imprisonment for AML and tax fraud offenses
